# Memory, Compaction and Persistence

This page describes how berg-agents remembers things across turns and
sessions, how it keeps the context window within budget, and where that
state lives on disk.

All of it is wired automatically through `build_chat_agent` in
`berg_agents/plugin_system/context_capabilities.py` --- no extra setup is
required.
The four capabilities are registered in a specific order; see
**Registration order**.

## What is in context every request

A bounded snapshot of `MEMORY.md` is injected beside the latest user
prompt, inside `<memory>...</memory>` tags, followed by a
`<memory_instructions>` block.
This snapshot is **refreshed on every
request** --- including immediately after a write or external edit --- so a
model that just saved a fact does not need to re-read the file to see it.

Only the main notebook is injected that way: other memory files appear
by name only, referenced through it.

| File on disk | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `{config}/memory/MEMORY.md` | The auto-injected notebook. Plain Markdown. |
| `{config}/memory/<topic>.md` | Append-on-topic files. Read only on request. |
| `{config}/memory.db` | SQLite fallback store when file-backed mode is unavailable. |
| `{config}/runs.db` | Paired with `StepPersistence` (see below). |

Where `{config}` is the resolved config directory (`.berg-config` /
`.berg-agents` / `~/.berg-agents`; see `CONFIGURATION.qmd`).

## Memory tools

The model can call the standard memory toolset:

- `write_memory` --- append a new durable fact (pass `old_text` to amend or
  remove one; de-duplicate instead of duplicating).
- `read_memory` --- for **topic files only**.
  Never for `MEMORY.md` itself;
  it is already in context and does not live inside the workspace.
- `search_memory` --- keyword lookup across memory files.
- `delete_memory` --- remove a memory entry.

The companion guidance (in `context_capabilities._MEMORY_GUIDANCE`) states
plainly that `MEMORY.md` is already present in context, which prevents the
observed failure mode of the model using `read_file`/`read_memory` to
re-fetch it and hitting "file not found".

## Writing and editing memory by hand

Because the canonical store is `FileStore`, `MEMORY.md` is ordinary
Markdown --- read it, edit it, grep it, or version-control the folder.
Changes show up on the next request, bounded by the snapshot limit
described below.

A previous nested-path bug left an earlier file at
`{config}/memory/.berg-agents/berg-agents/MEMORY.md`.
It was not deleted
automatically --- move or merge that content into the flat
`{config}/memory/MEMORY.md` if you want it.

## When memory stops being fully automatic (limits)

The `Memory` capability only injects a *bounded* snapshot.
Content past
the configured `max_tokens`/`max_lines` is truncated, with the tail
available through `read_memory` and `search_memory`.
So automatic injection
is the rule for the small, durable facts; pull-on-demand covers the rest.

## Compaction

Context compaction rewrites history in place so the request stays within
budget.
Berg-agents uses `TieredCompaction`: cheap zero-LLM tiers first,
summarisation last.

1. **DeduplicateFileReads** --- blanks every read that was later superseded
   by a newer read of the same file.
2. **ClearToolResults** --- blanks the oldest tool results, keeping the
   newest sets (`keep_pairs=3`).
3. **ClampOversizedMessages** --- head/tail-truncates a single oversized
   part (e.g. a runaway generation).
4. **SummarisingCompaction** --- one model call, reached only when tiers
   1-3 cannot reclaim enough (`max_messages=1`, `keep_messages=20`,
   `receipts=True`).

Tiered strategies report what they dropped as a receipt, so a compaction
reads as an explicit note rather than silent amnesia.
`ReportContextUsage`
emits used/window/fraction events after compaction, feeding the live
context gauge in the web UI.

`FallbackCompaction` and `WarnNearLimits` are available in the harness but
are **not** wired into the berg-agents chat path (they would risk
compacting twice).

**Threshold**: 80% of the model's context window (unknown local GGUF
endpoints fall back to 32K so compacting starts early).
Budget parameters
are configured through `BERG_AGENT_SUMMARIZATION_*` keys; see
`CONFIGURATION.qmd`.

### Registration order (load-bearing)

Compaction is registered **before** `Memory`: compaction edits history
persistently while the memory block is request-only, so a memory block
added before the rewrite would be discarded.
Do not reorder these when
extending the capability list.

## Persistence and recall of prior turns

- `StepPersistence(store=SqliteStepStore, agent_name="chat")` snapshots
  every settled step into `{config}/runs.db`.
- `ConversationSearch(SnapshotHistorySource(store), scope="conversation")`
  gives the model keyword recall across those snapshots, including turns
  that compaction has dropped.

Together these give the model a useful "what did we do earlier?" path
that does not depend on the raw context window.

## Conversation (chat session) persistence

Separately from memory, chat sessions are stored by
`berg_agents/ui/session_store.py` in SQLite (`{config}/chat_sessions.db`)
holding the **full `Conversation` JSON**, not raw message lists.
That is
what made restores reliable: the system-prompt warning is stripped from
restored conversations and each dumped message gets a namespaced id.

## Known gaps

- `LearningGate` / harness gating for the chat path is deferred, not
  yet routed.
- Skills/MCP exposed as adapter plugins are working but their status as
  "plugins" versus first-class configuration systems is still open.
- SQLite connections in the session store must be per-operation (not
  cached) to satisfy thread affinity under `asyncio.to_thread`; the doc's
  troubleshooting entry covers symptoms.
